data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences — communications lost during atmospheric descent; first telemetry from a Mars lander. Coordinates: NSSDCA.

First spacecraft to return atmospheric data during Mars descent. Communications were lost at touchdown, but the descent telemetry — pressure, temperature, and a partial atmospheric composition profile — fed the engineering models that Viking would rely on three years later.
First in-situ atmospheric profile of Mars during EDL — direct input to all subsequent EDL designs.

Mars 6 arrived on 12 March 1974. Its lander transmitted all the way down through the atmosphere — the first measurements taken inside the Martian air — but a fault in the electronics garbled much of the data, and contact was lost moments before touchdown in Margaritifer Terra.
One of four Soviet Mars craft of 1973
A model of a Soviet Mars spacecraft of this family on display, its large dish antenna on top.
12 March 1974 — data all the way down
The 1972 Soviet stamp for fifteen years of the space era: a lander on the surface of Mars.
